meta.name: Create pytest fixtures for database and TestClient

context.prd-excerpt:
Link Shelf is a local, single-user link store: no authentication, no multi-tenancy, no sharing.
From the PRD's tech-stack rationale, which is the direct reason this task exists and why the fixtures are shaped the way they are:
"SQLite rather than PostgreSQL so the whole project runs with no external service: a fixture that needs a database server running is a fixture that fails for reasons unrelated to what is being tested."
Every backend task in this project writes tests against these fixtures. layer_plan.json OC-002 names them: L3-002 (app smoke), L3-003 (POST /links), L3-004 (GET /links and the tag filter) and L3-006 (POST /links/{link_id}/tags). The default test policy is TDD, so each of those tasks writes a failing test BEFORE its implementation, and every one of those tests needs a database and a client.
The two fixture names below are not free choices. tests/test_list_links.py (L3-004) is already written and requests fixtures called `db_session` and `client` by those exact names. Renaming either breaks tests this task must not edit.
context.tech-stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI 0.110+ (which brings starlette's TestClient), SQLAlchemy 2.x, SQLite (file-backed, no server process), pytest 8.x, httpx (required at runtime by TestClient). Backend only - no frontend, no container runtime.

task.objective: Create tests/conftest.py providing two fixtures - `db_session`, a SQLAlchemy session against a fresh empty SQLite database created per test, and `client`, a TestClient for the FastAPI app with get_db overridden to yield that same session - so that every backend test runs against an isolated database and never touches the real link_shelf.db.

requirements.requirement:
Create file `tests/conftest.py` with exactly these imports:
from collections.abc import Generator
import pytest from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from sqlalchemy import create_engine from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, sessionmaker
import app.models # noqa: F401 - registers Link, Tag and LinkTag on Base.metadata from app.db import Base, get_db from app.main import app as fastapi_app
The `import app.models` line is required and is not decoration: without it `Base.metadata.create_all` creates no tables and every test fails with "no such table: links". Keep the `# noqa: F401` comment so a later reader does not delete it as unused.
The `as fastapi_app` alias is required: the project has a package named `app`, and binding the FastAPI instance to the bare name would shadow it.

Define the `db_session` fixture. It MUST be named exactly `db_session` - tests/test_list_links.py and tests/test_tag_links.py request it by that name:
@pytest.fixture(name="db_session") def db_session_fixture(tmp_path) -> Generator[Session, None, None]: engine = create_engine( f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'test.db'}", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}, ) Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) factory = sessionmaker( bind=engine, autoflush=False, autocommit=False, expire_on_commit=False, ) session = factory() try: yield session finally: session.close() engine.dispose()
Points that are load-bearing rather than stylistic:
- `tmp_path` is pytest's built-in per-test temporary directory fixture. Using it is what makes each test get its OWN database file, so no test can see another's rows. Do not use a module-scoped or session-scoped path, and do not add `scope=` to this fixture - the default function scope is the isolation. - A file-backed database under tmp_path, NOT `sqlite:///:memory:`. An in-memory SQLite database is per-connection, so the session and the TestClient request could end up looking at two different empty databases. A file avoids that entirely and needs no StaticPool juggling. - `expire_on_commit=False` must match app/db.py's SessionLocal. With the SQLAlchemy default of True, a test that commits a Link via db_session and then reads `link.id` triggers a refresh, and the failure looks like a handler bug rather than a fixture setting. - `connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}` is required because TestClient runs the app on a different thread from the test function, and both use this session. - `engine.dispose()` in the `finally` releases the file handle. Without it, Windows may refuse to remove tmp_path. - Do NOT register a `PRAGMA foreign_keys` listener here. app/db.py registers one on the Engine class, which covers this engine too.

Define the `client` fixture. It MUST be named exactly `client`:
@pytest.fixture(name="client") def client_fixture(db_session: Session) -> Generator[TestClient, None, None]: def override_get_db() -> Generator[Session, None, None]: yield db_session
fastapi_app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db try: with TestClient(fastapi_app) as test_client: yield test_client finally: fastapi_app.dependency_overrides.pop(get_db, None)
Points that are load-bearing:
- It takes `db_session` as an argument. That is what makes the client and the test share ONE session, so rows a test adds through db_session are visible to a request the client makes, and vice versa. Creating a second session here would give the test and the app two different views of the same file. - `override_get_db` must NOT close the session. Closing is db_session's job in its own teardown; closing here would shut the session after the first request and break any test that makes two. - Use `.pop(get_db, None)` in a `finally`, NOT `.clear()`. tests/test_list_links.py installs its own temporary override of `get_db` to exercise the read-failure branch of list-links#4; `.clear()` would also discard overrides a test is managing itself. The `finally` guarantees cleanup even when a test raises, so no override leaks into the next test. - `with TestClient(...)` rather than a bare constructor: the context manager runs the app's startup and shutdown events, which is what a real server does.

Define NO other fixture in this file. In particular do not add an `engine` fixture, a `tmp_db_path` fixture, autouse fixtures, or `pytest_configure` / `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hooks. Nothing in this plan asks for them, and an autouse fixture in conftest.py changes the behaviour of every test module in the project including the layer-3 ones this task must not disturb.

The fixtures must never touch the real database. `app.db.DATABASE_PATH` (<repository root>/link_shelf.db) must not be read, written, created or deleted by anything in this file. Do not import `engine`, `SessionLocal` or `init_db` from app.db - only `Base` and `get_db` are needed, and importing the others invites accidental use.

Do NOT modify any existing file. Not app/db.py, not app/main.py, not any model, and above all not tests/test_list_links.py, tests/test_save_link.py, tests/test_app_smoke.py or tests/test_tag_links.py. If a layer-3 test fails once these fixtures exist, that is a finding to report against that task, not a test to rewrite here.

task.test-requirements:
Test policy: TDD, runner pytest. Write tests/test_fixtures.py first, watch each assertion fail against the absent conftest, then write tests/conftest.py until they pass. The fixtures are the artefact under test here.
Create test file: `tests/test_fixtures.py`. This file tests the fixtures themselves, so it requests them by name like any other test module:
import pathlib
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from sqlalchemy import func, inspect, select, text from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
import app.db from app.db import get_db from app.main import app as fastapi_app from app.models import Link, LinkTag, Tag
Every test below cites NO acceptance criterion. No criterion in this PRD describes test infrastructure - see the note on <source-feature>.
Test: test_db_session_is_a_session_against_a_schema_with_all_three_tables - Signature: `def test_...(db_session: Session)` - Assert `isinstance(db_session, Session)` - `tables = set(inspect(db_session.get_bind()).get_table_names())` - Assert `tables == {"links", "tags", "link_tags"}` - exactly the three declared tables, proving `import app.models` in requirement 1 registered all of them - Assert `db_session.get_bind().url.database.endswith("test.db")` - a temp file, not the real database - Asserts requirements 1 and 2.
Test: test_db_session_starts_empty_and_accepts_writes - Signature: `def test_...(db_session: Session)` - Assert `db_session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Link)) == 0` - `db_session.add(Link(url="https://example.com/leak-probe", title="probe"))` - `db_session.commit()` - Assert `db_session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Link)) == 1` - Asserts requirement 2. This test deliberately leaves a row behind; test 4 proves it did not survive.
Test: test_db_session_is_isolated_from_the_previous_test - Signature: `def test_...(db_session: Session)` - Assert `db_session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Link)) == 0` - Assert `db_session.scalar(select(select(Link.url).where( Link.url == "https://example.com/leak-probe").exists())) is False` - This is the isolation guarantee, and it only means something because test 3 ran first and committed a row. Keep these two tests adjacent and in this order in the file. If this test fails, the `tmp_path` per-test database of requirement 2 has been replaced with a shared one. - Asserts requirement 2.
Test: test_db_session_enforces_foreign_keys - Signature: `def test_...(db_session: Session)` - Assert `db_session.execute(text("PRAGMA foreign_keys")).scalar() == 1` - Also assert the constraint actually bites: `db_session.add(LinkTag(link_id=999, tag_id=999))`, then `with pytest.raises(IntegrityError): db_session.commit()`, then `db_session.rollback()` - This proves the per-test engine inherited app/db.py's Engine-class pragma listener, which is why requirement 2 forbids registering a second one. Without it, L3-006's tests for tag-links#4 would pass against a database that silently permits orphan join rows. - Add `import pytest` and `from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError` to this module. - Asserts requirement 2.
Test: test_client_is_a_testclient_that_serves_the_app - Signature: `def test_...(client: TestClient)` - Assert `isinstance(client, TestClient)` - `response = client.get("/openapi.json")` - Assert `response.status_code == 200` - Assert `response.json()["info"]["title"] == "Link Shelf"` - the client is bound to app.main:app and not to some other application - This assertion is deliberately endpoint-agnostic: /openapi.json is served by FastAPI itself, so this test proves the fixture works without depending on L3-003's or L3-004's handlers being correct. - Asserts requirement 3.
Test: test_client_overrides_get_db_with_the_test_session - Signature: `def test_...(client: TestClient, db_session: Session)` - Assert `get_db in fastapi_app.dependency_overrides` - `override = fastapi_app.dependency_overrides[get_db]` - Assert `next(override()) is db_session` - the override yields the SAME session object the test holds, which is what makes rows added through db_session visible to a request - Asserts requirement 3. This is the assertion that would catch a re-declared `get_db`: the override would be registered under a different key and this lookup would raise KeyError.
Test: test_client_never_points_at_the_real_database - Signature: `def test_...(client: TestClient, db_session: Session)` - Assert `str(db_session.get_bind().url) != app.db.DATABASE_URL` - Assert `pathlib.Path(db_session.get_bind().url.database).resolve() != app.db.DATABASE_PATH.resolve()` - `src = pathlib.Path("tests/conftest.py").read_text()` - Assert `"DATABASE_PATH" not in src` - Assert `"init_db" not in src` - Assert `"SessionLocal" not in src` - Assert `"from app.db import Base, get_db" in src` - only those two names are imported from app.db, so the module-level engine can never be reached by accident - Asserts requirements 3 and 5.
Test: test_the_override_is_removed_after_the_client_fixture_tears_down - Signature: `def test_...()` - this test requests NEITHER fixture - Assert `get_db not in fastapi_app.dependency_overrides` - Place this test LAST in the file, after the tests that use `client`. It proves the `finally: dependency_overrides.pop(...)` of requirement 3 ran, so no override leaks into a later test module - which would otherwise make tests/test_list_links.py read from a database belonging to a test that has already finished. - Asserts requirement 3.
Test: test_conftest_declares_only_the_two_agreed_fixtures - `src = pathlib.Path("tests/conftest.py").read_text()` - Assert `src.count("@pytest.fixture") == 2` - exactly two fixtures - Assert `'name="db_session"' in src` and `'name="client"' in src` - the two names tests/test_list_links.py and tests/test_tag_links.py request - Assert `"autouse" not in src` and `"pytest_configure" not in src` and `"pytest_collection_modifyitems" not in src` - Assert `"memory" not in src` - the fixture uses a tmp_path file, not :memory: - Asserts requirements 2, 3 and 4.

verification.step: Run: `python -c "import tests.conftest; print('conftest imports cleanly')"` - must print `conftest imports cleanly`. Run this FIRST: a conftest that raises at import produces a collection error for the whole suite rather than a single test failure

Run: `python -c "import pathlib; src = pathlib.Path('tests/conftest.py').read_text(); assert src.count('@pytest.fixture') == 2; assert 'name=\"db_session\"' in src; assert 'name=\"client\"' in src; print('two fixtures, correct names')"` - must print `two fixtures, correct names`

Run: `python -c "import pathlib; src = pathlib.Path('tests/conftest.py').read_text(); assert 'DATABASE_PATH' not in src; assert 'init_db' not in src; assert 'SessionLocal' not in src; assert 'memory' not in src; assert 'autouse' not in src; print('isolation constraints OK')"` - must print `isolation constraints OK`, proving requirements 4 and 5
Run: `pytest tests/test_fixtures.py -v` - all 9 test functions pass

Run: `pytest tests/test_db.py tests/test_link_model.py tests/test_tag_models.py -v` - L4-001, L4-002 and L4-003 still pass, proving the new conftest did not disturb the layer-4 test modules that build their own engines

Run: `pytest tests/ -v` - report the full result. This is the task that resolves layer_plan.json OC-002, so layer-3 modules that were erroring on the missing `db_session` and `client` fixtures should now collect and run. Report any that still fail as a finding against the owning layer-3 task; do NOT edit a layer-3 test

Run, AFTER the full suite: `python -c "import app.db, sqlalchemy as sa; i = sa.inspect(app.db.engine); names = i.get_table_names(); rows = {t: app.db.engine.connect().execute(sa.text('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ' + t)).scalar() for t in names}; print(rows); assert all(n == 0 for n in rows.values()), rows"` - every table in the real link_shelf.db must have ZERO rows, proving no test wrote to it. The tables themselves may exist: L4-001's `test_init_db_creates_the_database_and_is_idempotent` calls `init_db()` against the real engine, and now that app.models exports all three models that call legitimately creates links, tags and link_tags. Empty tables are correct; any row is a fixture bypassing the get_db override
